author: John Gruber
description:
This page from Google Design on their “Material 3” UI language came to my attention after my snarky post about the ungainly new to-do app they bizarrely bragged about on Twitter/X this week. I don’t think this “Material 3” page is new — I think it’s a few years old — but I’d never seen it before.

First, it’s crazy that (in desktop browsers with a mouse cursor) they change the I-beam cursor for text selection to ... a circle. I guess it looks kind of fun but the whole point of the I-beam cursor is to enable precise character selection. They changed that to something that makes precise selection as difficult as possible. It’d be better to just an arrow pointer than a goddamn circle. This, from the UI design team.

Second, this paragraph made me honestly wonder if I was reading a spoof, a years-old unfunny April Fool’s
title: Google’s ‘Material 3’ Design Write-Up Is 93.3 Percent Embarrassing
